meta.title: OpenPlanner – video appointments with your team, booked in seconds
meta.description: OpenPlanner is the open-source scheduler for video calls on Webex. Participants pick a free time on a page in your branding, the call lands in Webex Contact Center, and personal data is gone 24 hours after the call.

hero.lead: OpenPlanner is the scheduler for video calls on Webex. A participant picks a free time on a page in your branding, gets a confirmation with a calendar invite and joins from the browser. No account, no app, no login. Your team receives the call at the right moment in Webex Contact Center, and personal data is gone 24 hours after the call.

tour.title: From click to call, and everything behind it
tour.lead: Two tracks through the product: what the participant experiences, from picking a time to the call, and what the team and the administrators hold, from the organisation to the agent who picks up.

steps.title: Picking a time
steps.text: Month calendar, free times of the day, a short form with three fields and the group's own questions. On your domain, in your branding.

steps.title: Or talk now
steps.text: When the group is open, the participant can call right away. A cap on the number waiting and honest queue feedback keep it tidy.

steps.title: Confirmation by email
steps.text: Confirmation with a calendar invite (.ics), the personal management link and the reminder later. By SMS if the group wants it. SPF, DKIM and DMARC checked.

steps.title: Move or cancel
steps.text: Through the personal link, without an account. Cancel until the start, move until an hour before; known details are filled in already.

steps.title: Test the video first
steps.text: A real trial call on Webex: camera, microphone and sound checked before it matters, with the result visible in the team's agenda.

steps.title: Starting the call
steps.text: Join from the browser, no app or account. Every appointment is its own Webex meeting; the participant waits in the lobby until the agent is there.

steps.title: One installation, several organisations
steps.text: Each organisation with its own groups, branding, texts, channels and identity provider. Roles from the IdP: superuser, organisation admin, group admin, planner, agent, auditor.

steps.title: Groups as skills
steps.text: A group is a skill: a subject, a team, a queue, its own opening hours and form. The participant never picks a person; the call goes to the first free agent.

steps.title: Staffing per block
steps.text: Blocks per day with the number of agents, holidays, exceptions and an emergency closure in one action. Capacity decides what the participant gets to see.

steps.title: Agenda and planner, live
steps.text: Every call with its status: planned, trial call done, in the call, finished. The planner moves or cancels on the participant's behalf and sees the reason of every failure.

steps.title: The work item at T−5
steps.text: Five minutes before the start the call lands as a work item in Webex Contact Center, or in OpenPlanner's own queue. Chosen per group, and switched when the contact center is down.

steps.title: The agent picks up
steps.text: With the agent role, the agent takes the call from the queue, sees only a first name and a subject, and joins the meeting as cohost. 24 hours after the call the data is gone.

steps.title: You set up a group
steps.text: A team is a group: opening hours, staffing per block, holidays, exceptions, texts and branding. All in the admin portal, no code.

steps.title: Your website links to the page
steps.text: Every group has its own page on your domain. Or you place the calendar as a Web Component right inside your own site.

steps.title: The call arrives by itself
steps.text: As a work item in Webex Contact Center, or in OpenPlanner's own queue where staff with the agent role pick up the call themselves. Chosen per group.

features.title: Everything a call needs, nothing that distracts
features.lead: Built for teams that serve many people by video: customer service, advisory desks, intake, helpdesks.

items.title: Booking without friction
items.text: Month calendar, free times, three fields. Move or cancel through a personal link. Works without JavaScript and fully by keyboard.

items.title: Webex built in
items.text: Every appointment gets its own Webex meeting. The participant joins from the browser, no app or account; your team joins as cohost.

items.title: Lands where your team works
items.text: The call goes to the queue in Webex Contact Center as a work item. The first free agent picks up. Nobody has to watch a calendar.

items.title: Talk now
items.text: A group that is open can offer a direct call, with a cap on the number waiting and honest queue feedback.

items.title: Multitenant with real roles
items.text: One installation, several organisations, each with its own groups, branding, texts and identity provider. Roles and scope come from your IdP; one authorisation matrix decides what everyone sees and does.

items.title: Groups as skills
items.text: A group is a skill with a subject, a team and a queue. The participant never picks a person; the first free agent picks up. One agent can be in several groups.

items.title: Privacy by design
items.text: Personal data lives only on the booking and is gone 24 hours after the call. Never in logs, URLs, jobs or error messages.

items.title: Your brand, your words
items.text: Colours, logo and font per organisation. Every text editable in the portal. Dutch and English out of the box, more locales possible.

items.title: Messages that arrive
items.text: Confirmation, change, reminder and cancellation by email (with .ics) and SMS. SPF, DKIM and DMARC are checked for you.

items.title: Agenda and planner
items.text: Admins follow every call live, plan staffing per block and close a group in one action when needed, after which participants pick a new time themselves.

integrations.title: Webex Meetings is the heart. Everything else connects to it.
integrations.lead: OpenPlanner is not a video platform and not a contact center. It is the scheduler that ties together the Webex products you already have, and keeps every other system behind a clean adapter.

items.name: Webex Meetings
items.text: Every appointment is a real Webex meeting through the Meetings API. Browser-direct join, a trial call beforehand, live meeting status in the agenda.

items.name: Webex Contact Center
items.text: Five minutes before the start the call becomes a work item in the team's queue, carrying only a first name, the join link and routing attributes. Webex Contact Center is the first integration; the layer behind it is provider-neutral, and a group can also work without a contact center through OpenPlanner's own queue.

items.name: Webex Messaging
items.text: A bot tells administrators in Webex when the integration falters, a queue fills up or a check fails. Never personal data, always a link to the portal.

items.name: Your identity provider
items.text: Administrators sign in through your own IdP (PingFederate, Keycloak, Entra ID, any OIDC provider), per organisation, with roles from the claims.

items.name: Email and SMS
items.text: SMTP and a provider-neutral SMS gateway per organisation. Texts per channel and per group editable in the portal.

items.name: AI agents and bots
items.text: A contact-center bot (such as the Webex AI Agent) asks for free times and books on the participant's behalf through an API with scopes and per-client keys.

integrations.roadmap: Other contact-center platforms on the same adapter layer (ADR 0032), the calendar invite as a third dispatch kind (ADR 0043), changes through the bot API (ADR 0023) and staff through SCIM (ADR 0046).

enterprise.title: Why we call OpenPlanner enterprise-ready
enterprise.lead: Not because of a list of ticks, but because of how it is built: a core without a framework, every external service behind a port, and rules the pipeline enforces instead of a reviewer.

plate.title: Architecture plate: what runs and what goes where
plate.lead: One server you manage yourself, two containers and one database. Everything outside it is a system you already have, connected through an adapter.

flows: The participant books over HTTPS; the data stays in the database on your server.
The worker creates the Webex meeting and sends the confirmation and reminders by email or SMS.
Five minutes before the start the contact center gets a work item with only the first name, the join link and the routing attributes.
Administrators sign in at your own identity provider; every decision goes to the audit log, which you can ship to your own log systems.
Updates arrive as signed images; the host updater checks the signature before it switches.
plate.caption: Simplified. The full plate, with every flow and the decision behind it, is in the repository.

enterprise.arch_caption: The arrows point one way. On every pull request import-linter refuses an import that breaks these layers.

layers.name: Domain
layers.note: Pure Python, no framework, ≥ 90% test coverage

pillars.title: One core, replaceable edges
pillars.text: Another contact center or video platform is a new adapter behind an existing port. The domain, the screens and the texts do not change.

pillars.title: Enforced, not agreed
pillars.text: Layers, types, rights and privacy rules are checked on every pull request. What does not hold never reaches main.

pillars.title: One source per subject
pillars.text: Rights, settings and the portal's structure each live in one place; their documentation is generated from the code.

pillars.title: Recorded decision by decision
pillars.text: More than eighty ADRs with context, choice, settings and build status. An architect reads why things are the way they are, and what does not run yet.

scale.title: Now: one host, well above the design target
scale.text: Proxy, web and worker on one VM with SQLite in WAL mode. Readers do not block each other, a booking is a few rows under a write lock, several workers share the job queue. One installation serves many organisations. Scaling is vertical first: more CPU, memory and a faster disk.

scale.title: A recorded limit
scale.text: The design target is about 80 bookings per working day. ADR 0036 records when we go further: above 2,000 bookings per working day, at a p95 above one second, with a stricter availability requirement, or when a client requires managed Postgres.

scale.title: After that: designed, not built yet
scale.text: Postgres with row locks, several web instances behind the proxy, workers on any host and shared storage for rate limits. All database access already sits behind one port in one adapter module, so the domain, the routes and the screens stay the same.

scale_link.label: ADR 0036: scaling envelope and the path beyond one VM

items.title: One authorisation matrix
items.text: Role × permission × level in one place. Every admin route declares one permission, every query filters by scope, every denial is in the audit log. No exception for superusers.

items.title: Multitenant, separated per organisation
items.text: Every query filters by the role's scope; an organisation admin never sees another organisation, a group admin never another group. The same matrix drives the menu, the buttons and the API.

items.title: Single sign-on, no detour
items.text: OIDC with PKCE, state and nonce, asymmetric algorithms only, eight-hour session. No local accounts, no break-glass login, on purpose.

items.title: An audit log you can forward
items.text: Logins, changes and denials as structured events, to syslog, Splunk or Elastic. Without personal data.

items.title: Signed releases
items.text: Images signed keyless with cosign, an SBOM (CycloneDX) on every release, CVE scans with trivy and grype, hashes in the lockfile. The installation verifies the signature.

items.title: A strict pipeline
items.text: mypy strict, ruff, bandit, semgrep, gitleaks, mutation testing, schemathesis, OWASP ZAP, Playwright with axe-core and Lighthouse. Everything blocks the merge.

items.title: Light to run
items.text: Two containers, one SQLite file, HTTPS with automatic certificates or your own proxy. Updates and release channel from the portal. The backup is one file.

items.title: Accessible, provably
items.text: WCAG 2.2 AA on every public page, in every language, tested again on every pull request. No time limits, no CAPTCHA puzzles.

items.title: Configurable, not hard-coded
items.text: Every threshold, limit and period is a setting with a class, a default and bounds. What is a protection cannot be switched off from the portal.

opensource.title: Open source, open decisions
opensource.lead: OpenPlanner is published under the EUPL-1.2, the open-source licence of the European Commission. Not only the code is open: every design decision sits in the repository as an ADR, with what has been built of it.

points.title: EUPL-1.2
points.text: Use, change and distribute it, commercially too. Compatible with GPL, AGPL and most European procurement rules.

points.title: Architecture Decision Records
points.text: More than eighty decisions, each with context, choice, settings and build status. You read why things are the way they are, and what does not run yet.

points.title: Security up front
points.text: A threat model per flow, an abuse case per endpoint, each with a test. Responsible disclosure through SECURITY.md.

points.title: Contributions welcome
points.text: Issues, discussions and pull requests on GitHub. A CLA keeps the licence clean. Every PR answers the same seven review questions.

releases.title: Releases
releases.lead: Every merge to main becomes a release candidate on the rc channel. A release is a signed image, an SBOM and this website, in one train.
releases.none: No release on this channel yet.
releases.built: This page was built from commit {commit}.
releases.no_data: The release list is read from GitHub on every build; this local build has none.
releases.fresh: On every merge to main and on every release this page is rebuilt with the releases of that moment. Your browser never talks to GitHub, which keeps this site free of third parties.

cta.title: Put it on a test server this afternoon
cta.text: One install script, a Let's Encrypt certificate and a demo group. Or start locally with docker compose and walk the portal as every role.

footer.tagline: Video appointments with your team, booked in seconds, privacy by default.
footer.nocookies: This website sets no cookies, uses no trackers and loads nothing from third parties.
footer.license: Source code under EUPL-1.2. Made by 3Corners and the OpenPlanner contributors.

standards.title: Quality and standards, provably
standards.lead: What we claim is in the code, in a test or in the pipeline. For each standard you see how far it is and where the evidence is.
code: Python 3.12 with full type checking (mypy strict) and ruff for style and common mistakes.
A layered architecture, enforced with import-linter: the domain knows no framework.
Every module and function with a Google-style docstring, readable by documentation tools.
Test coverage ≥ 90% on the domain and translations, mutation score ≥ 80%, abuse cases as tests.
Conventional Commits, one ADR per decision with its build status, and every PR answers seven review questions.
bandit, semgrep, gitleaks, pip-audit and a licence check on every pull request.
update: The superuser picks the channel in the portal: stable, or release candidate for a test environment.
Install a new version with one click in the portal, or let the installation do it by itself.
The host verifies the signature of every image before the update; an unsigned image does not run.
Renovate keeps dependencies current weekly, security updates at once; a PR older than 14 days raises an alert.
Database migrations run automatically and can always be rolled back.

items.name: WCAG 2.2 AA (EN 301 549)
items.what: Keyboard flow, axe-core with zero violations and Lighthouse ≥ 95 on every public page, in every language, on every pull request. Manual audit with NVDA and VoiceOver before go-live.

items.name: NL Design System
items.what: Colours, type and spacing of the participant pages come from NL Design System tokens; organisations adjust them within those tokens.

items.name: HTTPS, HSTS and NCSC TLS guidelines
items.what: HTTPS with HSTS (Forum Standaardisatie comply-or-explain list), TLS 1.2 and 1.3 per the NCSC guidelines. A check in CI and internet.nl in the go-live checklist are planned.

items.name: SPF, DKIM and DMARC
items.what: Comply-or-explain standards for email. The portal checks each organisation's sender domain and shows what is missing.

items.name: OpenID Connect
items.what: Administrators sign in through their own identity provider: PKCE, state and nonce, asymmetric algorithms only. Tested against Keycloak, PingFederate in production.

items.name: OpenAPI 3
items.what: The API specification is generated from the code, compared on every pull request and attacked with schemathesis.

items.name: GDPR and privacy by design
items.what: Personal data only on the booking, purged 24 hours after the call, never in logs. The data-flow diagram is the input for the organisation's DPIA.

items.name: Building blocks for the BIO
items.what: An audit log of every change and denial, security events on attacks, an auditor role and export to your log platform. The BIO itself remains the organisation's responsibility.

items.name: security.txt (RFC 9116)
items.what: A fixed reporting point for vulnerabilities on every installation, with SECURITY.md in the repository.

items.name: Software supply chain
items.what: Every image signed keyless with cosign, a CycloneDX SBOM with every release, CVE scans with trivy and grype, dependencies pinned with hashes.

items.name: Standard for Public Code
items.what: EUPL-1.2, a licence per file through REUSE, decisions public as ADRs, and a publiccode.yml that CI validates and every release updates. The listing on developer.overheid.nl is still open.

items.name: Penetration test
items.what: An external penetration test before go-live and yearly after. Until then: OWASP ZAP on every merge and abuse cases as tests.
